S-RTK.NAME: rtk
S-RTK.core-purpose: High-performance command proxy that filters command output, preserves exit codes, tracks savings, supports hooks, and reduces LLM-visible shell output.

key-surfaces.surface-1: src/main.rs defines the CLI command router across git, JS/TS, Python, Go, Rust, cloud, system, analytics, and hooks.
key-surfaces.surface-2: src/core/runner.rs provides shared execution, filtering, passthrough, streaming, and tracking skeletons.
key-surfaces.surface-3: src/core/filter.rs provides source-code filtering levels and language detection.

strengths.strength-1: Best preserved as a sidecar boundary: fast, mature, language-specific, and already tracks savings.
strengths.strength-2: Fits Reasonix shell tool and terminal command workflows without replacing the agent loop.
strengths.strength-3: Can expose savings telemetry to MAGRA dashboard through `rtk gain` or history DB reads.

integration-obligations.obligation-1: Add RTK policy to Reasonix shell execution: auto-prefix supported commands, allow raw bypass, preserve exit code and approval gates.
integration-obligations.obligation-2: Surface RTK savings in dashboard status/usage views without hiding raw-output recovery.
integration-obligations.obligation-3: Detect missing or wrong RTK binary in doctor/health checks.

risks.risk-1: Blind auto-prefix can alter command output shape expected by tests or scripts; policy must be per-shell-tool output, not arbitrary user scripts.
risks.risk-2: RTK installed version may differ from source version; diagnostics must report both when relevant.
risks.risk-3: Bundling Rust binaries raises packaging and platform support work.
